item.title: Opinion | Massive national forest project needs a closer look at impacts, alternatives
item.description: The Forest Service must take a more careful look at the project’s impact on the adjacent Sturgeon River Gorge Wilderness, surrounding state and private lands, and the long-term health of the Ottawa National Forest.

item.title: Michigan town keeps zoning blocking trustee’s gravel mine
item.description: A northern Michigan township official wanted to end zoning, which would help him build a gravel mine. The township board just said no.

item.title: Michigan falls behind in race to save disappearing farmland
item.description: Thousands of farms and hundreds of thousands of acres of farmland have been lost to development and other economic pressures in recent years. Michigan does less than most to stem the tide.

item.title: Tech group: Michigan will be sued over efforts to restrain social media
item.description: A major tech group suggests Michigan would be sued if it tries to regulate minors’ access to social media. State lawmakers are undeterred.

item.title: Ice shanties & ear stones: A day in Lake Michigan’s last whitefish stronghold
item.description: Photos from southern Green Bay’s world-class ice fishing scene help tell the story of ongoing efforts to protect the iconic Great Lakes whitefish.

item.title: A Wisconsin whitefish refuge offers lessons for Michigan. But will it last?
item.description: Once considered too polluted for whitefish to thrive, southern Green Bay has suddenly become the only place in Lake Michigan where the fish aren’t collapsing. What can Michigan learn from its success? And will it last?

item.title: Lansing gridlock jeopardizes licenses for 8K Michigan doctors
item.description: Doctors say Michigan patients can expect longer wait times if an interstate agreement isn’t signed. Members of both political parties blame each other for the stalemate.

item.title: Longer sentences push Michigan prisons closer to capacity
item.description: Michigan’s prison population has begun to rise slightly after years of decline, bringing correctional facilities closer to full capacity as the number of available beds shrinks following recent prison closures.

item.title: Case closed on Michigan’s ‘false electors.’ Dana Nessel won’t appeal dismissal
item.description: Michigan's attorney general won't pursue appeal after a court dismissed charges against a group of Republican 'false electors' who falsely claimed Donald Trump won Michigan in 2020.

item.title: Aric Nesbitt includes more state psychiatric hospitals in anti-crime agenda
item.description: Michigan needs more psychiatric hospitals to cut down on homelessness and crime, the GOP gubernatorial candidate has proposed, coinciding with a Trump administration push for more institutionalization of the homeless.
